title: AI linked to 84% of ransomware attacks, new report finds
key_facts: Semperis's 2026 Ransomware Risk Report polled 1,200 IT and security professionals in nine countries.
84% of surveyed ransomware victims said attackers used AI in the attack; 44% said attackers exploited their own AI systems.
69% had multiple successful attacks in the past year; 59% paid a ransom at least once; 87% saw attacks on identity systems.
More than a third faced psychological or physical threats against employees.
Chris Inglis, former US National Cyber Director and Semperis board member, says autonomous ransomware attacks are already happening.
Inglis says the weakness that lets attackers in is usually the same as before AI and that defenders must use AI too.
quote_evidence: Cybercriminals exploited artificial intelligence in ransomware attacks experienced by 84% of surveyed victims, according to a sweeping new global cybersecurity report.
I think we're already seeing autonomous attacks.
why_it_matters_hint: A vendor survey suggests AI is now part of most ransomware attacks, though it is self-reported and from a security vendor.
notes: Survey by a security vendor, Semperis, which also employs the quoted experts (Inglis sits on its board); figures are self-reported by respondents.
